EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  JUNE 25, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:01 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Bill Kemp
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 29, 2018
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MAY 29, 2018 ADJOURNED
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, inquired about the completion of the new judges booths
in Ernie Howlett Park. She noted that the Horse Show Judges Booth between Arenas #1 and
#2 was difficult to use by judges due to the double windows configuration. The Community
Services Director reported that the City was still waiting for bay windows to be installed at no
cost to the City by a volunteer from the Peninsula Committee – Childrens Hospital and would
contact them again to determine the installation date. Ms. Schachter also noted that there
were minor items to complete in the new Dressage Judges Booth.

Tracy Johnson, 15 Sorrel Lane, inquired when the footing material in the Dapplegray Park
main arena would be replaced and also requested one additional jump standard to form an
oxer. The Community Services Director responded that the arena was scheduled to have the
footing replaced in the new fiscal year and would inform the City’s Maintenance Supervisor
that an additional set of jump standards was needed at this arena.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 25, 2018  1
 Bob Fritz, 14 Pony Lane, informed the Equestrian Committee that the equestrian/pedestrian
street crossing with a yellow blinking light poles was not stopping traffic when riders or
pedestrians were in the Rolling Hills Road crossing. He recommended that the City review
the speed limit sign placement on the northbound (downhill) side of the road as a possible
source for blocking drivers’ views and for the City to cut back the low hanging limbs and
shrubs on the east side of the crossing approach area. The Community Services Director
thanked Mr. Fritz for his information and stated that the potential speed limit sign obstruction
would be reviewed by the City’s Traffic Safety Engineer and that the City’s Maintenance crew
would cut back the low limbs and shrubs on the east side of this street crossing.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Korey Bradbury and Korina Winji from California Water Service Company distributed and
reviewed an agreement being provided to horse owners impacted by the Water Reliability
Project along the City’s bridle trails where new water pipes will be installed. Ms. Winji
indicated that the temporary boarding agreement was developed from the feedback received
from horse owners who would need to temporarily relocate their horses.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL indicated concern about a W-9 form that was required to be
completed and the short timeline to relocate horses, due to some local stalls being considered
for relocating horses needing renovation before horses could be safely boarded. Mr.
Bradbury indicated that Dapplegray School was going to be a project staging site for its
equipment and pipeline materials. He also assured residents attending the meeting that
Phillips Canyon Trail will remain open during the project.

Bob Fritz, 14 Pony Lane, indicated concern about just receiving California Water Service’s
temporary boarding agreement and having to move horses in four days. He provided
information about his family’s search for enough boarding stalls to accommodate their large
horses and horses in foal at Peter Weber Equestrian Center and Palos Verdes Stables. Mr.
Fritz indicated that if he could take his horses in and out of the front of his property, he would
not need to relocate them. However, California Water Service Company has told him this is
not a safe option.

In response to MEMBER SILVANO’S inquiry, Ms. Winji confirmed that the relocation boarding
agreement was on a month-to-month basis. Mr. Bradbury stated that most horses would
need to be relocated for approximately six months. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL thanked the
California Water Service Company staff for attending this meeting and updating the
Equestrian Committee on this important project.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CITY CELEBRATION VENUE UPDATE
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL briefly reported that the City Celebration Subcommittee had met
earlier that evening and discussed the City Celebration’s schedule of events at The Empty
Saddle Club and the Remember the Music Festival’s set-up and schedule at Howlett Park.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 25, 2018  2
 THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CHANDLER PARK TEMPORARY VIDEO CAMERA UPDATE
The Community Services Director provided an overview of the Chandler Park arena usage
statistics. Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, stated that she has had to board her horse at
the Peter Weber Equestrian Center and use this facility’s arenas due to the overcrowding in
the Chandler Park horse arena. MEMBER SHINN stated that she believed that the level of
arena use at Chandler Park justified consideration of adding a second arena in this park.
Discussion ensued of whether the second arena was needed or whether to enlarge the
current arena.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO ALLOW THE EXPANSION OF THE
  CHANDLER PARK HORSE ARENA.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

The Community Services Director clarified that the Equestrian Committee will discuss this
recommendation further at the July 30, 2018 Committee Meeting before forwarding it to the
Park and Activities Commission.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported on a recent Subcommittee meeting with Alexa Davis, Assistant to
the City Manager, and Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst, who had recently completed
her new position’s orientation that will include coordinating the City’s emergency
preparedness program. MEMBER SHINN reported that a horse chipping clinic was being
considered for August 4, 2018 at the Peter Weber Equestrian Center, if Gil Houle would
approve. In addition, a trailering clinic organized by Sean Martin would soon be held, equine
“go bags” for emergency evacuations were reviewed, and a future Equestrian Response
Team (ERT) Level 1 course would be hosted in the City Hall Council Chambers once enough
interested residents had completed the prerequisite on-line course.

The Community Services Director noted that John Douglass had indicated that there was no
formal plan developed for equine emergencies or evacuations for the Palos Verdes
Peninsula. MEMBER SHINN stated that the Subcommittee should begin to identify several
evacuation locations around the Peninsula to take horses during a local disaster or fire.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 25, 2018  3
 HIGH SCHOOL EQUESTRIAN TEAM
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL reported to the Equestrian Committee that a letter of concern to be
sent to the Palos Verdes Peninsula School District would be discussed at the June 26, 2018
City Council meeting.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, reported that the Colina Lane HOA fencing along
  the Howlett Trail needed replacement.

  MEMBER SHINN stated that she would contact the First Baptist Church of Palos
  Verdes regarding the removal of their fallen fence along the Botanical Gardens Trail.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

C.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK JUDGES BOOTH COMPLETION – July 30, 2018

D.  PROPOSED EXPANSION OF CHANDLER PARK HORSE ARENA – July 30, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING TO
JULY 30, 2018.

The meeting adjourned at 8:20 p.m.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 25, 2018  4
 Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
